name: Purnananda
dates_notes: A Bengali Śākta author active in the sixteenth century; *Śrītattvacintāmaṇi* is conventionally dated 1577, but biographical dates are not secure.
core_thesis: Pūrṇānanda is the sixteenth-century Bengali Śākta author of the *Śrītattvacintāmaṇi*. Its sixth section, the *Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa*, became an especially influential textual presentation of six principal cakras, the channels, and the ascent of kuṇḍalinī in the early modern reception of Tantra. The work should be read as a historically specific Śākta synthesis, not as an unqualified description of a single pan-Indian or timeless yogic system. This record therefore names the text's structural contribution while reserving its detailed practice claims for source-verified treatment.

engaged_works.title: Sritattvacintamani
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Standardly transmitted as Pūrṇānanda's Śākta compendium.
engaged_works.summary: A Śākta compendium in twenty-six sections. The sixth, *Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa*, presents a subtle-body and cakra sequence that became highly influential in later global accounts of kuṇḍalinī; a printed Sanskrit text and translations exist, but no verified local primary witness is linked here.
